title: Compiled transition without a nondeterministic choice
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program, let $l_0$ be its initial label, let $D$ be a deterministic machine with $k_D$ work tapes, and let $q_0$ assign a state of $D$ to each of the $d$ deciders. For any compiled state $q$ at which $A$ offers no nondeterministic choice, and for any bits $b$ and $\beta$, the transition of the compiled nondeterministic machine under $b$ at $q$ equals the transition of the deterministic compilation obtained by replacing each choice instruction with the return value $\beta$.
hypotheses_covered: A is a nondeterministic register program
D is a deterministic k_D-tape machine
q₀ assigns a state to each of the d deciders
q is a compiled state with no available choice
b and β are Boolean choice/return values
